clue.text: Man's work -car, if a T model, taking time

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form, so these letters are moulded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A motorist builds his own car on the lines of Ford's old Model T, taking his time over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' reshapes CAR IF A T into ARTIFAC, and T for 'time' is added at the end. 'Model T' looks like the Ford car, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object made by human hands, as opposed to something natural.

clue.text: Tell a Roman Catholic girl

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to inform a girl who belongs to the Roman Catholic church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' looks like a verb, but it is William Tell, the legendary Swiss bowman who shot an apple off his son's head.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tell is the most famous bowman of Swiss legend.

clue.text: Upholding art? Cast is worthless

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding something up means its letters run upwards, reading from bottom to top

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast

explanation.surface: Someone defends a work of art, but the cast of the show is judged no good.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Upholding' turns the art upward; 'Cast' looks like a theatre company but is a verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy goods are rubbishy and of no value.

clue.text: Showing it hurts when jaw is put in a cast

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the jaw going within the throw

parts.note: a fling is a throw or cast
the chin is the lower part of the jaw

explanation.surface: Someone with a broken jaw winces when it is set in plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests a plaster cast, but here it is a throw, FLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Wincing or recoiling is the reflex of someone in pain.

clue.text: Remarks made about chap — top dog — giving orders

indicators.note: the remarks go round, or about, the other pieces

parts.note: comments are remarks
a man is a chap

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Comments are passed about a man who is top dog and fond of giving orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top dog' looks like a boss, but 'top' only takes the first letter of 'dog'; 'about' wraps the remarks round the chap and that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ten Commandments are divine orders, and the word means any authoritative instructions.

clue.text: Links carriers out East with this fly

indicators.note: the letter for East is taken out of the word for golf bag carriers

parts.note: on a golf links, caddies carry players' clubs

explanation.surface: Golf caddies out in the eastern part of the course are bothered by a fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Links' is a golf course, so its carriers are CADDIES; dropping E leaves the insect name.
explanation.definitionFit: The caddis fly is an insect whose larvae build protective cases underwater, much used by anglers.

clue.text: Brief account — the boy's played his part

parts.note: AC is the short form of account
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A short report says the boy did his share of the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to perform a role on stage, so having acted is having performed one's role.

clue.text: Act the lackey to gain authority

parts.note: to do is to act
a minion is a servile lackey

explanation.surface: A servant behaves obsequiously in the hope of winning power.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion is sovereign power or control over people or territory.

clue.text: Guide-line for colours

definitions.meaning: a benchmark or rule to go by
a flag, and regimental colours are flags

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a norm or criterion to follow; the other is a banner carried by troops, which soldiers call their colours.

clue.text: Mad March is a powerful influence

indicators.note: mad suggests wild disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Like the March hare, madness in springtime exerts a strong pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' scrambles MARCH IS A; 'Mad March' recalls the mad March hare.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is personal magnetism, an attractive power over others.

clue.text: Street-girl's pedigree

parts.note: Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl who lives on the street has a family tree after all.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemma is a family tree or line of descent.

clue.text: Accidentally gored, hear am to be taken to hospital — having bled a lot

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: an accident throws things into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bullfighter gored by accident tells someone he'll go to hospital after losing much blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accidentally' rearranges the eleven letters of 'gored, hear am', and the hospital letter goes in front; 'having bled a lot' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A haemorrhage is a heavy escape of blood, so to have haemorrhaged is to have lost much of it.

clue.text: Principle of the change in command

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of these letters

parts.note: IC stands for in charge, or in command, as in 2IC

explanation.surface: Someone asks what lies behind a reshuffle at headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges 'the'; IC (in charge) is a crossword stand-in for 'in command'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral rule or belief guiding conduct.

clue.text: Unrestrained derelict

definitions.meaning: wild, uninhibited, given over to impulse

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is wanton or uninhibited behaviour; the other is a building or vessel left by its owners.

clue.text: Monsieur made trouble, giving offence

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up or disturb, so these letters are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: A Frenchman caused a disturbance and committed a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdemeanour is a minor wrongdoing or crime.

clue.text: Noted aces spinning yarns

indicators.note: spinning sends these letters whirling into a new order

explanation.surface: Famous experts tell tall stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' rearranges NOTED ACES; 'spinning yarns' is also storytelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarns are tales told for entertainment, just like short amusing stories.

clue.text: Certain trees requiring identification, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly tells us the words are heard spoken, not read

parts.note: trees whose identity is unknown prompt the question which elms

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to tell particular trees apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Asking 'Which elms?' identifies elms; spoken, the question sounds like the name of the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The wych elm is a particular species of elm tree native to Britain.

clue.text: Bus-lane diversion around post-office novice driver ignored? Summons follows!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the post office
a traffic diversion reroutes, so these letters take a new order
the learner is left out of the bus lane letters

parts.note: taken as written
L is the learner driver's plate
PO is the abbreviation for post office

explanation.surface: A bus-lane diversion near the post office, ignored by a learner driver, leads to a court summons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' drops the learner plate from the bus lane, 'diversion' shuffles what remains, and 'around' places the post office inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A subpoena is a writ requiring someone to appear in court.

clue.text: Certainly not the fruit of the elder

definitions.text: Certainly not the fruit of the elder

parts.words: Certainly not the fruit of the elder
parts.note: the elder seems to be the elderberry tree, but it is an older person, whose offspring would not be junior fruit

explanation.definitionFit: Youngberries are a hybrid blackberry fruit, and the name says they are young rather than elder.

clue.text: A fine, healthy state to be in

definitions.text: A fine, healthy state to be in

parts.words: A fine, healthy state to be in
parts.note: the phrase hints at the idiom for being in good form, a fine condition someone is said to be in

explanation.definitionFit: Fettle means condition, almost always heard in the phrase 'in fine fettle', meaning healthy and spirited.

clue.text: Comments that one player does not direct to another

definitions.text: Comments that one player does not direct to another

parts.words: Comments that one player does not direct to another
parts.note: an actor on stage sometimes speaks remarks to the audience that the other characters supposedly cannot hear

explanation.definitionFit: In theatre, a remark spoken to the audience and unheard by fellow actors has its own name.

clue.text: Game to put an ingredient of beer with whisky?

parts.note: a hop is the flower used to flavour beer
Scotch is whisky from Scotland

explanation.surface: A brewer adds hops to whisky and calls it a game.
explanation.walkthrough: HOPSCOTCH is a children's playground game of hopping through chalked squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground pastime of hopping through squares.

clue.text: Many praise him

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: Lots of people speak highly of a certain man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' is the definition: the answer is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Claud is a man's name, so a male person referred to by the pronoun.

clue.text: Straighten the line of the garment

definitions.meaning: a frock, an item of clothing

explanation.definitionFit: Military drill uses the word for aligning a rank, and it is also a woman's frock.

clue.text: Play in general on the street

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general
a way is a road or street

explanation.surface: A general is spotted at play out in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' is slack or freedom of movement, as in a rope with some play in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room for manoeuvre, slack or free play.

clue.text: Panicking serviceman died, going round the art gallery

indicators.note: the serviceman and died go round the gallery

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, so a serviceman is a GI
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A soldier collapses and dies while touring a gallery, causing panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' wraps A GI and D around TATE, the London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated means flustered and nervously disturbed, the state of a panicking person.

clue.text: In addition, chary about drink

indicators.note: the wary word is placed about, or around, the joining word

parts.note: chary means wary or shy
and means in addition

explanation.surface: Besides, someone is cautious about having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a light drink.

clue.text: Doctor Seuss — do you initially name Homer's hero?

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered
initially means take the first letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A question to the children's author about naming the hero of Homer's epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb, not Dr Seuss's title: it rearranges SEUSS, DO and Y, the first letter of 'you' given by 'initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus is the hero of the Odyssey, Homer's epic poem.
